title: The Frog in the Well
text:
A frog lived in an old, broken down well. One day a great turtle from the Eastern Sea passed by, and the frog called up to him, delighted to show off his home.

How happy I am here, the frog said. I can hop up onto the edge of the well and rest in the gaps of the broken bricks. I can swim in the water up to my armpits, and wade in the mud up to my ankles. Look at the crabs and tadpoles: none of them can match me. I am master of all this water and all this well. Why not come in and see for yourself?

The turtle tried. But before his left foot was even in, his right knee was already stuck fast in the narrow opening. He backed out carefully and told the frog about the sea.

Its width, he said, could not be measured in a thousand miles, nor its depth in a thousand fathoms. In the time of the great Yu there were floods nine years out of ten, and the sea did not rise. In the time of Tang there were droughts seven years out of eight, and it did not sink. That was the joy of the Eastern Sea.

When the frog heard this, he was struck dumb with astonishment and felt very small indeed.
lesson: What you can see from where you stand is not the whole world. Before declaring yourself the best or calling something impossible, find out what lies outside your well.
people: A frog, a turtle of the Eastern Sea
